messages.content: What belongs in a paired image-edit example?
A source image, an edit instruction, and a reviewed target image.
An edit preserves everything but misses the requested change. Is it successful?
No. The requested edit must visibly happen as well as preserving unrelated content.
Can a small pixel difference prove that a semantic edit succeeded?
No. Inspect instruction fulfillment and scene preservation separately.
Can validation images be replayed as training successes?
No. Keep evaluation groups and their asset hashes excluded from training.
A target image has extra fingers. Is this a clean training target?
No. Flag the anatomy error for review instead of accepting the target.
Is this text-only starter an image editing corpus?
No. It illustrates review policy; real image training needs licensed source and target pixels.
